registered_by: coordinator, before implementation and before any measurement of it
why_not_prc1: PR-C1 (Squad C) moves the step boundary to the lane tail. Reading the code to implement it shows it is not safely completable as a patch: it requires the commit to move off the seal, which in turn requires availability.inserted and sealed_rows to move to queue time (the duplicate-offer hazard those exist to prevent), a flush before every owner read (multi_writer.rs reads its own private objects mid-save), and a flush in finish_inner - and it needs a batch bound, where the only existing candidates (capacities.transaction_rows = 8191, batch_objects = 512) hold the arbitration lock 340x longer than today and would reproduce the #209 second-writer failure. PR-C1 is not refuted; it is larger than a patch and under-specified in its bound.

root_cause_refinement.statement: The amplification is a FORMAT property, not a cadence one. pack/layout.rs directory_is_starts_only() is true for PackLane::WholeFile alone, and the WholeFile lane is the lane with 51.21x amplification. Its directory grows with every append, so every body moves, so append_pack must rebind the entire pack (cas/placement.rs:203-205 states this). Fixing that at the root - a directory-last layout, or reserved directory space - is a Store-format change and needs an explicit owner ruling. This campaign does not propose one.

treatment.one_difference: A lane that seals after every record stops retaining an open pack: after placing a group, the lane closes its pack instead of keeping it open for a later append. The predicate is exactly the set selection.rs:57-58 and :97-102 already uses to seal per member - WholeFile | PooledMetadata | Singleton. Nothing else changes: same groups, same records, same group grammar, same commit cadence (one commit per seal, unchanged), same pragmas, same capacities, same worker count, same durability, same rack limits.
treatment.rationale: A retained open pack only pays for itself if a later group appends to it. For a lane that seals one group per record, every later group appends exactly once and each append rewrites the whole pack, so the retained tail is a pure loss on that lane: it converts one insert of the new group into a rewrite of up to PACK_LIMIT. Closing the pack turns each write into insert_pack of that group alone.
not_changed: no capacity, policy constant or PRAGMA
no commit cadence - commits stay per seal
no arbitration lock hold change - one lock per seal as today
no Store format: a single-group pack is already well-formed and PackLane::Singleton emits exactly that shape

compared_against.why: it is the most recent diagnostic row carrying the pack counters this treatment moves (packs_created, pack_appends) as well as the profile buckets, on the same product source and the same harness instrumentation

expected_movement.pipeline.profile_commit_ns: 1,145,315,268 -> ~350-700 ms (fewer bytes to flush; the per-commit fixed cost is unchanged)
must_not_move: the row's PASS status and all 13 gates
may_move_and_must_be_reported: the store file hash - pack boundaries change page and freelist layout

refuted_if: rewritten bytes do not fall below 1.0 GB
sql_ns + commit_ns fall by less than 300 ms while the counters move as predicted (the page-flush model is then refuted for this row)
any pinned counter or the filesystem root moves
the row fails any gate, or the harness registry self-check regresses
any of pack_locator, pack_watermark, visibility, cas_reuse, persistence_failure, multi_writer goes red
the complete command exceeds the 15 s budget (the reference row is 4.79 s)
known_risks: pack rows rise ~13x, so object_packs goes from 1,250 to ~16,800 rows and packs_save grows with it; each write that creates a pack also runs UPDATE saves SET pack_ceiling and, because next_pack_id moves every step, advance_pack_if_moved writes store_policy. Both are hot single-row pages, so this treatment ADDS up to two dirty hot pages per commit (~142 MB of extra flush over 17,378 commits) while removing ~1.99 GB of pack rewriting. The trade is expected to be strongly positive but the added statements are real and are reported.
the read path loses the benefit of a warm 256 KiB pack holding many whole-file objects; the pack cache is dropped per write either way (cas/placement.rs:217).
